channel.title: Hill Mole — The Audio Edition
channel.description: Hill Mole, Chris Abraham's serialized confession novel, read aloud in full: every chapter as audio, in order, in one feed. The text edition lives at hillmole.com, and the whole book, text and audio together, is on one page at hillmole.com/complete.html. This feed is the novel as a listening series.
channel.itunes:author: Chris Abraham

item.title: Chapter 309: Fighting firearms with firearms
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator applies Frank Luntz’s point that what people hear matters, arguing news about mass shootings makes people buy high capacity rifles.
item.content:encoded: Simple NLP: the more the news says “bad people mass shooting with high-capacity rifles” the more people hear “I need to buy a gun but not a pistol or shotgun or hunting rifle, I need to buy a high-capacity firearm with high capacity magazines in order to defend against a dangerous world requiring sustained firepower and possibly multiple assailants.” To quote Frank Luntz, “it’s not what you say, it’s what people hear.”

item.title: Chapter 308: America’s fragile democracy
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that when people say democracy is fragile, they mean their own plans are, since democracy also elects people they oppose.
item.content:encoded: Authoritarianism is the only way anyone can keep the pendulum from swinging. A painful majority of Americans don’t currently agree with the current arc of history. That shows in laws, the court, elections. Do you want to blow America up to prevent that? I think you surely do? When folks say “democracy is fragile” I believe that means “our plans are fragile” rather than American republican representative democracy (where the chips fall where they may) is fragile. That democracy isn’t fragile. But that durable democracy does include presidents like Trump and justices like Kavanaugh, which is #notmyamerica which means that sort of democracy is as fragile as hell unless America implements authoritarianism. Then, America’s democracy will be fucked but the liberal vision for America will be as sound as a pound. Amen.

item.title: Chapter 307: Ashli Babbitt
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator asks why accounts said five people were killed at the Capitol when the only person shot was Ashli Babbitt, and what that says about belief.
item.content:encoded: My question is why does the January 6 narrative insist backwards and forwards that 5 people were killed at the Capitol? One casual scratch at that and it’s only Ashli Babbitt. What’s the compulsion? To prove that people will believe anything they’re told? And people do believe it, too. Even with a Washington Post article saying otherwise. I’m amazed by the human mind and the human mob mentality, even though it’s always on display.

item.title: Chapter 306: Total retribution
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short entry arguing that much Republican activism against Democrats is simply retribution for years of efforts to restrict guns and ammunition.
item.content:encoded: I honestly think that most Republican activism against Democrats is just to get back at them for constantly going for their guns and ammo. Total retribution.

item.title: Chapter 305: Twenty percent of Americans trust their government
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator notes that with 400 million guns and only one in five Americans trusting the government in 2020, America is playing a dangerous game.
item.content:encoded: 80% of Americans would rather be Brazil than Australia; also, none of those countries have any real “natural rights granted by God not to be infringed,” only rights granted to them by their governments only when convenient. Fair weather friends. 400 million guns, most of those ARs. This is a dangerous game since only 20% of all Americans say they trust the government as of 2020. Which means 8 out of 10 do not. Hillbilly Americans are not an outlier no matter what the New Yorker experiences from within their bubble.

item.title: Chapter 304: Gun crimes always drive gun sales in America
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator notes that gun crime boosts gun sales and carry permits rather than bans, recalling stores sold out of Glock 19s after the Giffords shooting.
item.content:encoded: An increase in gun crime always drives gun sales and applications for carry permits in America rather than driving gun restrictions or gun bans. Unintended consequences gone wild. First aware of this in the wake of the shooting of Gabby Giffords in 2011. I was driving cross-country and checked all the gun stores and everyone was out of Glock 19s, the weapon the shooter used. Plus, lawsuits end up in courts that result in gun prohibitions being loosened. Every time.

item.title: Chapter 303: Disinformation Governance Board
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator asks whether the federal Disinformation Governance Board, not called counter disinformation, produces disinformation or reduces it.
item.content:encoded: The new organization is not called “anti-disinformation” or “counter-disinformation,” it’s just called the Disinformation Governance Board. Does that mean disinformation producer or disinformation reducer?

item.title: Chapter 302: Chest seals in your go bag
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: Reading about the Spanish Civil War, the narrator notes that the people he knows with chest seals in their go bags are all on the political right.
item.content:encoded: I was recently reading about the Spanish Civil War and the sexy, heroic, fraternal, liberals were decimated by the fascist nationalists but they always thought they were the most righteous and most deserving to win and on the right side of history until they were completely crushed into cinder. 100% of the people I know who have chest seals in their go bags are on the right. Just saying.

item.title: Chapter 301: Sacrifice for the collective
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues America has not prized sacrifice for the collective since the 1930s, not even in World War Two, favoring isolation and greed.
item.content:encoded: In America, “sacrifice for the collective” hasn’t been an American virtue since the 30s—not even during war, including WW2. We were extremely isolationist and extremely reticent, and waiting until the 11:59th (23:59th) hour. More of a “greed is good” ethos.

item.title: Chapter 300: Populist democracy versus constitutional republic
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that the left treats America as a populist democracy while the right sees a constitutional republic where popular votes matter less.
item.content:encoded: I finally get why leftists are so frustrated with fighting conservatives in the elections: the left believes they live in a populist democracy and the right realizes it lives in a constitutional republic. Popular votes mean almost nothing in the American system of government.

item.title: Chapter 299: Ukraine brainwashing
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short entry asking whether the Russian people, the European people, or the American people are the ones brainwashed about the war in Ukraine, or all of them.
item.content:encoded: Are the Russian people brainwashed? Are the European people brainwashed? Are we, the American people, brainwashed? All the above?

item.title: Chapter 298: Decriminalize crime
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: In a satirical entry, the narrator proposes making illegal things legal so there will be fewer criminals and fewer people in jail, a glass half full view.
item.content:encoded: I figured it out: decriminalize crime! That’s what folks want. Or, redefine what crime is and what criminal is. If you can strike down crimes and make formerly illegal things legal–or, not illegal–then there will, indeed, be fewer criminals and fewer people in jail. I’m into it. Let’s try this and see what happens. I’m a glass-half-full, prison-half-empty kind of guy.

item.title: Chapter 297: Free speech isn’t equitable speech
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that equitable speech means someone chooses whose voice is amplified and whose is suppressed, which is power, not equality.
item.content:encoded:
Free speech is not necessarily equitable speech. What people want seems to be equatable speech. Who gets to choose? Nina?

Until I meet an actual Philosopher King or King Solomon, then equity is just thumbs on scales. It’s basically Cyrano.

It’s basically bias dressed up as equity. The power is in who gets to choose whose voice is worthy of amplifying and whose voice is worth suppressing.

That’s what equity is.

That’s equality for authoritarians. Egalitarianism for folks who are afraid of losing control of their own power, or perceived power.

The old tail wagging the dog schtick.

item.title: Chapter 296: Dear Powers-that-Be
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that relying on censorship, moderation and calling things misinformation shows leaders have lost the trust of their people.
item.content:encoded: : if you really need to rely this much on suppression, moderation, censorship, and dismissing everything as misinformation, disinformation, and conspiracy theory, then it’s because you’ve completely lost the trust and control of your people, your culture, your narrative, and your leadership.

item.title: Chapter 295: Killing’s come a long way since 1945
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator lists how far the technology of killing has come since 1945, from nuclear weapons and drones to smart bombs and targeted biologicals.
item.content:encoded: The technologies to kill efficiently have come a long way since 1945. Nukes exist. Biologicals can be targeted to DNA. Satellites exist. Subs are better. There are jets now. Helicopters now. Drones now. Smart bombs. Not even the AR or AK existed in 1945. So much potential death!

item.title: Chapter 294: Slavs don’t grok articles in English
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator jokes that you can tell messaging from Ukraine or Russia because native speakers drop English articles, so follow the articles.
item.content:encoded: You can tell if the messaging is coming from Ukraine or Russia because all the articles will be missing from Russian sentences. No matter how smart the Ukrainian or Russian, they really just can’t figure out the Articles. Neither can the Poles, either. The entire region can’t sort out English Articles. All the rest are written by Team America Propaganda Inc or Five Eyes Storytellers LTD. Look for the articles. Ask Fox Mulder. It’s not “FOLLOW THE MONEY” anymore it’s “FOLLOW THE ARTICLES!”

item.title: Chapter 293: Vainglory
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues Putin sees NATO expansion as a broken promise, lost the moral high ground by invading Ukraine, and that humiliating him risks escalation.
item.content:encoded: Putin will go to the mat, whatever that looks like. Words like “humiliate” and “glory” always end up in the official announcements in English on Pravda and Tass. To these organs, the West, funded by the USA, has slowly disrespected the verbal agreement that was made in 1997 over NATO never expanding beyond former East Germany. I wish more people knew that Putin doesn’t see any part of this invasion the way anyone in the West seems to. Now that he’s invaded Ukraine, no matter the reason, Putin has relinquished any moral high ground. Even so, nobody believes Putin can be shamed back into compliance; instead, humiliation can truly result not only in escalation but in a nuclear war. Putin plans to go to the mat on this. I know some people know what’s actually happening, from the Russian perspective, however, it’s not remotely part of the official narrative. The popular story. In Putin’s reality, he’s a very patient man who finally had to put his foot down. That he was fully baited, since 1997, into doing this. And he will never back down. So this is going to be extremely dangerous. In this scenario, Putin’s 1940 Japan, Ukraine’s Pearl Harbor, and the USA and Europe have slowly put a noose around Russia’s neck. That’s what Putin thinks is happening here and painting him as simply a vainglorious madman is extremely good for propaganda but if it’s what people really think in the Pentagon and in Brussels, then that’s terrible intel.

item.title: Chapter 292: Are we the world, are we the children?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator calls the wave of we are the world messaging about Ukraine uncritical propaganda, and says he is against war and democracy by force.
item.content:encoded: The level of shameless we are the world propaganda is so rich, thick, endless, and uncritical of itself that it’s stressing even me out and I’m probably a nihilist and nonplussed by most global behavior. My only constant is being profoundly anti-war but also being profoundly anti “liberal democracy by force” as well. It’s a direct analog to a sort of 11th century Crusades, just replacing Rome with America (fuck yeah?). It’s crazy-making to me. I’m not listening to the news anymore. Yikes!

item.title: Chapter 291: These are the buds of the socialist spring
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short entry quoting a passage about Ukraine’s famine, a dead mother and nursing infant at the Kharkiv market, and the bitter phrase people used.
item.content:encoded: “One spring morning, amidst the piles of dead peasants at the Kharkiv market, an infant suckled the breast of its mother, whose face was a lifeless gray. Passersby had seen this before . . . that precise scene, the tiny mouth, the last drops of milk, the cold nipple. The Ukrainians had a term for this. They said to themselves, quietly, as they passed: ‘These are the buds of the socialist spring.’ ”

item.title: Chapter 290: Consensus reality generators
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: Listening to an old Art Bell show, the narrator enjoys the idea that television, film, science fiction and news work as consensus reality generators.
item.content:encoded: Listening to an old Art Bell radio show and they discussed TV and movies as consensus reality generators, especially science fiction and speculative fiction and even news reporting. So fascinating as a concept and as a conceit. Love it!

item.title: Chapter 289: The slave would rise in rebellion
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short entry quoting Callicles in Plato’s Gorgias on the strong man who throws off society’s laws and lets the light of natural justice shine.
item.content:encoded:
“But if there were a man who had sufficient force, he would shake off and break through, and escape from all this; he would trample under foot all our formulas and spells and charms, and all our laws which are against nature: the slave would rise in rebellion and be lord over us, and the light of natural justice would shine forth.”
—Callicles

item.title: Chapter 288: I’m not remotely an enemy of Russia or Putin
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues Putin has been restrained and America has committed worse, and that Russia now holds Europe hostage through natural gas.
item.content:encoded: I think he’s been amazingly restrained. We’re the baddies. He’s been amazingly patient and exceedingly clear where his line in the sand is. And we’re in a glass house with our incessant war crimes since at least 2001. Putin’s an amateur. A little polonium sushi versus two AGM-114 Hellfire on every Predator drone. And how America has killed more civilians with our economic sanctions than ever with guns and bombs and missiles. Putin is smart: Russia’s a biosphere and it’s self sufficient now because we’ve been playing these games against Russia for long enough for Putin to adapt. Right now, America is impotent. Putin has all of Western, Central, and Eastern Europe by the balls over natural gas. It’s a perfect storm and if we’re not careful, Putin will humiliate us publicly and it’ll be impossible to recover our face. I like when that happens. A shamed America is a less violent America. Vietnam did a number on us and we were too shell shocked to war monger for a good twenty years, twenty five years. With the humiliation of the Afghanistan retreat added to the public spanking we’ll probably soon get, coordinated, from China and Russia, it’ll be really interesting to see what the future holds with regards to American hegemony.

item.title: Chapter 287: Not even one dirty bomb in 72 years is suspicious
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator suggests that decades without a single nuclear attack or dirty bomb are suspicious, and that the threat may have been used for control.
item.content:encoded: When it comes to nuclear threat and even the true existential threat from the former Soviet Union, when nothing happens or has happened or had happened, then I always assume it was just staged for publicity. For power, manipulation, and control. Not even one good nuclear attack or dirty bomb in the last 72 years is extremely suspicious.

item.title: Chapter 286: How fucked is Germany right now?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator describes Germany’s bind: it dropped coal and nuclear power, became dependent on Russian gas, and now faces a war over Ukraine.
item.content:encoded: Dumping coal and nukes in their transition to renewables and getting stuck with Russian gas in a time when gas couldn’t be more expensive and “war is imminent with Russia” over Ukraine with only the Nord Stream and Nord Stream 2 pipelines the only leverage that Biden has to work with, which would fuck Germany even more. Herr Olaf Scholz, dust off the nukes if you know what’s good for you. Plus, German <3 coal (lots of old buildings still have coal burning stoves). Viel Glück!

item.title: Chapter 285: Do I really think that Russia isn’t a bad actor?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that Russia has been encircled by Western bases since 2014, drawing on his trips over Russia in 1991 and to Saint Petersburg in 1996.
item.content:encoded: Do I actually think that Russia isn’t actually a bad actor that needs to be handled with a leader, Putin, who needs to be muzzled by the west? I do believe that, yes. With all my heart. I have since 1991 when I flew over Russia heading to Nepal and then in 1996 when I spent a lot of time in Saint Petersburg. Russia has always been a poor, under-resourced peasant nation with a few modern cities. Especially during the cold war and all the way back to tsarist Russia. First of all, we’ve had our boot on the neck of Russia since at least 2014, with a necklace of intimidating Western military bases and missile silos surrounding it as if Canada and Mexico had their missiles pointed at the USA. Sphere of influence disrespect. Also, I’ve been in international consulting for 20 years and work with Russians all the time. Tech Bros from Moscow, hot consultants from Moscow, loads of people. Hell I even have friends in Tehran. America is a liar. I’m always more likely to trust our so-called enemies. America needs to convince me it’s not lying about war. They’ve lied a million times since the Gulf of Tonkin. The USA is a liar that might tell the truth. Baseline. Iraq, Afghanistan, Contras, Yemen, Syria, Iran. Jesus! Globally, we’re the worst! Thank God we have nukes, good geographical placement, and the dollar. Otherwise, we’d have been actually spanked a million times. With crimes against humanity, with war crimes, war criminals. The reason we haven’t is because we’re untouchable.

item.title: Chapter 284: Covid modalities
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator sees two camps in America: those who think COVID is the worst thing in the world and those who don’t, each side mutually appalled.
item.content:encoded: I finally see that there are two dominant modalities in the USA and never the twain shall meet: folks who believe that COVID is the worst thing in the world and folks who think it isn’t remotely the worst thing in the world. They just don’t understand each other: COVID kills children, says one side; pish posh says the other. No comprehension. They’re both completely mutually appalled.

item.title: Chapter 283: Americans immune to being called Nazis
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator worries that accusations of racism or Nazism have become so common that many Americans now shrug them off completely, which scares him.
item.content:encoded: I never thought that the United States would ever become culturally immune to being called racist or Nazi or White Supremacist or Hitler but I think I was wrong. I think I am seeing Ronald Reagan-level Teflon against these ubiquitous accusations and refrains. Scares me.

item.title: Chapter 282: Spotify 451
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator calls the boycott of Spotify over Joe Rogan mob mentality, and argues that anything labeled dangerous should be read and preserved.
item.content:encoded: Class action boycott against Spotify over Joe Rogan? Tyranny! That’s why we have senators and electoral college and why America is a Republic: to avoid this sort of mob mentality. That said, very amusing to watch. Anything that brings more attention to folks actually watching and listening to anything red labeled as “dangerous misinformation and disinformation that will kill people” is pretty important to keep accessible and available. Historically, one should search out and quickly buy, read, and preserve the sort of history, literature, essays, interviews, and autobiographies that the authorities want to keep you from. Fahrenheit 451-level fun. I can’t believe I get to see it with my own eyes! This is great. And they’re blaming “public health” and “your own safety” and “to protect you” for it—which is classic dystopian schtick. This is priceless! I don’t care about Joe Rogan, per se, as I’m not even a regular listener, but this is happening all over YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, so my interest is more Jungian, more about Rogan as archetype. As the face of the oppression. Here’s the thing: I fancy the tyrants don’t even see their tyranny when they look in the mirror. They are doing this, as far as they’re concerned, honestly and selflessly paternalistically sacrificing themselves at the altar of saving us from ourselves. Because it looks like, to them, that we’re trying to kill ourselves and them with our selfishness about the masks and the vaccines and the pseudoscience and the horse worm protocols. They’re willing to break all the freedoms because there are lives at stake and we people are apparently both suicidal and okay with manslaughter. I get it but it’s not okay. It’s wrong.

item.title: Chapter 281: Maus
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator says readers of Maus learn that every holocaust begins differently and subtly, led by people you trust, like a slowly heating pot.
item.content:encoded: People who read Maus realize that not every holocaust will look the same and that every holocaust starts uniquely, subtly, organically, and pretty benignly, generally initiated by people you admire and trust. It’s not a switch. It’s a cool pot of water sitting on a low flame. It happens right under your nose, especially if and when you’re being willfully ignorant and actively blind.

item.title: Chapter 280: Wrong speech
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator satirizes the idea that wrong speech must be suppressed like a disease, comparing that urge to Stalinists, Maoists and the East German Stasi.
item.content:encoded: There’s right speech and there’s wrong speech. Right speech should be protected and amplified and codified; wrong speech, on the other hand, wrong speech needs to be suppressed and cauterized—and is always obviously objectively bad!—before infecting, like cancer, like plagues! Of course, the issue might be that this is how the Stalinists, the Maoists, and even the retro-cool Stasi Ossis! This is authoritarian-think. It’s pretty trendy right now. Dead sexy. Cold War Chic.

item.title: Chapter 279: Embargoes and Sanctions
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that sanctions on Russia echo the embargoes that pushed Japan toward Pearl Harbor, and that they can bait a country into war.
item.content:encoded: We’re putting the boot on the neck of Russia the same way we put our boot on the necks of Germany and Japan, baiting them into war. Best way to start a war? Embargoes and sanctions. Then you can blame them for attacking Pearl Harbor, if you will. It’ll be fun to see how Russia behaves as we tighten the sanction noose.

item.title: Chapter 278: Nikita Khrushchev’s Cold War The Musical
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short satirical entry hoping Vladimir Putin is well paid for his role in a revival of Nikita Khrushchev’s Cold War, The Musical, since the first was a farce.
item.content:encoded: I hope Vladimir Putin is being extremely well compensated by the USA for his role in the upcoming revival of “Nikita Khrushchev’s Cold War The Musical.” The first one was a farce too.

item.title: Chapter 277: Booster Shot
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A one-line entry asking whether the American military buildup in Central and Eastern Europe is mainly an economic stimulus, a works program.
item.content:encoded: Would I be too cynical if I suggested that the entire military buildup of US troops in Central and Eastern Europe is just a works program to boost and bolster the economy?

item.title: Chapter 276: The Hague
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that an International Criminal Court accusation is almost a badge of honor, since superpowers and their allies face no enforcement.
item.content:encoded: We live in a world where being accused of crimes against humanity by the International Criminal Court is more of a badge of courage than an international damnation because there’s effectively zero enforcement if you’re either a superpower or under the protection of one. And it kind of paints you as the sort of monster you really don’t want to fuck with.

item.title: Chapter 275: How climate mitigation will actually work
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator predicts humans will do as little as possible about climate change, and that a slow population collapse will hit the poorest hardest.
item.content:encoded: You want to know what humans will do to mitigate a global climate collapse? As little as humanly possible. You know how climate change will be mitigated? A climate-related Thanos event. That’ll take care of the mitigation. Unlike Thanos, that population collapse will not be sudden atomization, it’ll be extremely gnarly and obviously directly impact the most vulnerable and raze equatorial and southern hemispheric land masses with extreme ferocity. Yikes.

item.title: Chapter 274: Actual weapons systems are 30 years in the future
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator assumes real weapons run thirty years ahead, recalling an uncle at TRW who showed him particle beam weapon material back in 1986.
item.content:encoded: I just assume that kinetic weapons are secretly all 30 years in the future. Back in the 80s, my TRW Uncle from Los Angeles showed me his practical surface to air particle beam weapons. The 80s! Not theoretical but actual. 1986. I mean, they were beam weapons and they were pulsed because otherwise it would just cut through whereas when they pulse, they were catastrophic. That’s 35 years ago. And that’s for real. He gave me a TRW promotional pamphlet at the time. Wow, right?

item.title: Chapter 273: Everything dies baby that’s a fact
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator puts 1,500 COVID deaths in one day beside the roughly 7,000 Americans who die every day of every year, for perspective and proportion.
item.content:encoded: While 1,500 Americans passed of COVID-19 today, we tend to forget we’re mortal beings and that 7,123 die in America every single day of every single year, year in and year out, for perspective and proportion.

item.title: Chapter 272: The Trauma Wars
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that in America every family carries stories of trauma, which is why so many came, making a contest of suffering hard to win.
item.content:encoded: When you live in an immigrant nation like the United States, every family has its own stories of extreme trauma and suffering. That’s mostly why people used to come to America. Not just to become richer but to escape every version of trauma imaginable. It’s extremely hard to win the Trauma Wars when America is a traumatized country with epigenetic trauma out the wazoo.

item.title: Chapter 271: Noble lie
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short definition of the noble lie, a myth knowingly spread by an elite to keep social harmony or advance an agenda, from Plato’s Republic.
item.content:encoded: In politics, a noble lie is a myth or untruth, often, but not invariably, of a religious nature, knowingly propagated by an elite to maintain social harmony or to advance an agenda. The noble lie is a concept originated by Plato as described in the Republic.

item.title: Chapter 270: Nerds are never really cool even if they’re the elected leaders
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator compares politics to high school, where student government and grades never brought real power, and nerds grow heavy handed when ignored.
item.content:encoded: High School National Merit Scholars may have full control of the PA and the paper but that doesn’t mean they have any real power in the school. School cool runs in different rivers than student government or GPA. Same thing with real life. Nerds only think they lead. It is so annoying when they realize that life is just like high school because college isn’t like the real world or high school. When they realize how often they’re being defied or ignored, they can often become very insistent, even heavy-handed, which just makes things even worse.

item.title: Chapter 269: The state of American vigilantism
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator suggests Americans may not be against vigilantes at all, after a lifetime of films, books and video games that celebrate them as heroes.
item.content:encoded: Assuming Americans are anti-vigilantism might be wrong-thinking. America has been fed a diet of pro- vigilantism on film, television, novels, and video games since forever. I don’t know if Americans are even remotely anti-vigilante. Be careful. How are Americans programmed on this really? Be honest.

item.title: Chapter 268: Redeeming your enemy’s heroes
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that ubiquitous phone video cuts both ways: it proves what happened, redeeming everyone’s heroes and damning everyone’s enemies.
item.content:encoded: The good thing about panopticon citizen journalism and the ubiquitous filming of altercations is that the footage is proof of what happened so it’s almost impossible to manipulate the truth or influence outcome with testimony; however, the terrible thing about panopticon citizen journalism and the ubiquitous filming of altercations is that the footage is proof of what happened so it’s almost impossible to manipulate the truth or influence outcome with testimony. When things are political, the actual truth cuts both ways. It doesn’t only redeem your heroes and damn your enemies but it redeems everyone’s heroes and damns everyone’s enemies.

item.title: Chapter 267: Justifiable homicide
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator quotes a legal definition of justifiable homicide: killing in reasonable fear of death or great bodily harm, or to stop a violent felony.
item.content:encoded: A homicide is justifiable when committed in self-defense by one who reasonably believes that he is in imminent danger of losing his life or receiving great bodily harm and that the killing is necessary to save himself from that danger or when committed for the purpose of preventing a violent or forcible felony involving danger to life or of great bodily harm by one who reasonably believes that such an offense is about to be committed and that such action is necessary for its prevention. The circumstances must be sufficient to excite the fear of a reasonable person that there would be serious danger to his own life or person if he attempted to prevent the felony without the killing.

item.title: Chapter 266: Dear activists
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator warns that constant accusations of bigotry may one day make people embrace those labels, and wonders if that has been the goal.
item.content:encoded: it’s a dangerous blind spot to assume that your vision of the future is anyone else’s. I see a future of diminishing returns as people tire of being accused of bigotry, racism, sexism, jingoism, and xenophobia. Beware the date and time when they, instead, embrace their bigotry, racism, sexism, jingoism, and xenophobia. It always starts with “no matter what I say or do, you’re going to say that about me anyway, so I might as well…” That’ll be a scary day. Sometimes I wonder if that has been the goal the entire time? It’s amazing what you can make your enemy do if you bait them for long enough. Taunting always eventually results in some form of (filmed and posted) violence. If that’s the case, then slow-clap. Nefarious but genius. Long cons are the best cons.

item.title: Chapter 265: Gun v fist
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator explains that most American states do not require proportional force, so a gun may legally be used against an attacker using fists.
item.content:encoded: In US self defense law, there’s no expectation that you can’t defend yourself with deadly force or a firearm even if you’re defending yourself from a beating using fists and kicks. There are places in the world where there’s a requirement of proportionality, but not in most American States. You can fire on someone who’s coming at you with their fists. You don’t need to put down your firearm if it’s fisticuffs and get into your boxing stance. You can use a gun to stop yourself from getting beat up.

item.title: Chapter 264: Critical race theory
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that saying Virginia schools don’t teach critical race theory sounds evasive, since CRT is a lens that shapes how history is taught.
item.content:encoded: Even dumb hicks know that CRT is a lens through which history is interpreted and taught in school and not actually something that is actually taught in school. Any clever parry that “Virginia does not teach CRT in K-12 public schools.” It comes across as sneaky and sus. Even dumb hicks can see through that rhetorical sleight of hand. It’s too clever by half.

item.title: Chapter 263: A lifetime on the hips
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: Any time an elite calls ordinary Americans rubes, the narrator warns, opposition researchers will find it and it will cost votes at election time.
item.content:encoded: Any time or any place that an intellectual or elite calls a salt-of-the-earth American a Rube, it will be discovered and shared by Oppo. There’s no safe space for contempt, not even on podcasts. Fair warning. It’s a “moment on the lips, a lifetime on the hips” situation. And those add up and always blow back during the elections. And the Right does monitor everything the Left does. They have more stomach for that than the Left has for monitoring the Right, including churches, AM talk and forums.

item.title: Chapter 262: The hill they’re willing to die on
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator once expected gun confiscation to spark civil conflict in America, but now thinks vaccine mandates may be the true breaking point.
item.content:encoded: If America was ever truly vulnerable to actual “civil war,” I thought that the straw that broke the camel’s back would be gun confiscation but it actually might be vaccine mandates. I have never seen more people on that side of the aisle who are willing to die on that hill. Vaccine mandates might just be the hill they’re truly willing to die on.

item.title: Chapter 261: Eat me, Drake equation
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator answers the Drake equation with a joke: we are proof of life in the universe, and to believe anything else is just earthling supremacy.
item.content:encoded: Any time I wonder if there is life in the universe, I just look in the mirror. I am proof that there is life in the universe; you are proof that there is life in the universe. We’re of the universe. To believe anything less is to verge on geocentrism. The universe isn’t apart from us humans; nature isn’t apart from us humans, either. Anything else is earthling supremacy. Are you an earthling supremacist?

item.title: Chapter 260: The progressive pendulum is swinging right
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator predicts a conservative backlash after the 2020 protests and riots, with more policing and law and order voters, not defunding.
item.content:encoded: I feel like the long con perpetrated on the fine people who protested Floyd will be way more police rather than defund the police. Why? Because Americans lose all their fucks if they feel unsafe, insecure—or inconvenienced, even. There’s going to be some extremely conservative blowback to the perceived lawlessness that happened in the form of protests, riots, and tent cities. There will even be marijuana blowback. Mark my words. America’s a pendulum. Trump’s presidency was just the tip of the iceberg. All my little coal mine canaries are going from progressive poster children to NIMBY law and order voters. There will be blood. It’ll be a bloodbath.

item.title: Chapter 259: The Press is doing a Lazarus
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that print, radio and television are trying to protect their dominance by pushing to censor social media and online platforms.
item.content:encoded: So, let me get this straight: print, radio, and television has a plan to protect its narrative hegemony by censoring social media and internet platforms? Makes sense to me. Monopoly say what? Totally a monopolist thing to do: discredit, undermine, demonize, and destroy the competition using the laws and tools of the government to repress and suppress unapproved or countermanding narratives. Sounds like it’ll totally work.

item.title: Chapter 258: It’s the invisible hand
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator sarcastically questions whether rising meat and fuel prices are pure market forces or a nudge toward plants and away from fossil fuels.
item.content:encoded: The price increase of animal protein couldn’t be social engineering, it surely must be purely invisible-hand economic. This isn’t a so-called “nudge” towards plant-based nutrition through putting animal products financially out of reach of most people. That’s ludicrous… and brilliant! Same with fossil fuels: it’s the market, stupid. The inflation’s temporary. Issues of trade and logistics only. Chill?

item.title: Chapter 257: Don’t ever let the people think for themselves
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator asks if Facebook’s 2018 change toward friends’ posts was later called radicalization because people could no longer be filtered.
item.content:encoded: Didn’t the 2018 algorithm Facebook update empower users’ shares over media shares, in response to users’ request to see their friends’ timelines? So, basically, empowering users is, basically, radicalization because you can’t rely on folks’ unfettered, unfiltered, perceptions, beliefs, hopes, dreams, and subjective truths and facts. Am I close? Is that what happened?

item.title: Chapter 256: Ivermectin
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: Without endorsing it for COVID, the narrator argues that experts who called ivermectin only a horse dewormer lost public trust by saying so.
item.content:encoded: I am not on team Ivermectin but every time a smart person like a doctor or scientist who knows better calls a human medicine only a horse dewormer, they lose public trust. It’s way too sketch. It’s so suspicious. Only idiots ever thought that Ivermectin was only a horse dewormer. I assume everyone who called Ivermectin a horse dewormer (which it is, but not remotely only one) was stupid. Unless it was really clear that there were eye-rolls, humor, and snark. Otherwise, idiot. Oh well, I am just sharing. Whether or not it is actually an effective COVID-19 therapy is immaterial, it’s just not merely a horse dewormer the same way that Alprazolam isn’t a treatment for car and dog anxiety. Yikes, you chowderheads!

item.title: Chapter 255: Friends feeding frenzy
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator describes watching some of his smartest friends get swept up in mob mentality, and finds it fascinating, troubling and maddening.
item.content:encoded: It’s been interesting watching more than a few of my smartest friends (some of the brightest people in the world) on all sides fall head over heels for so much mob mentality. Watching them close their nictitating membrane and initiate an ocular rotation then join feeding frenzies I’m always surprised to see them caught up in, roiling in the turbulent bloody waters. It’s fascinating. It’s troubling. It’s maddening. It’s frustrating. None of you guys, of course! You’re fine. You’re all too smart to get baited into anything like that! Heavens no!

item.title: Chapter 254: Yelling fire in a crowded theater
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues the familiar fire in a theater line misreads the law: rights don’t excuse crimes, but speech is not banned in advance either.
item.content:encoded: When you use “you’re not allowed to yell fire in a theater” in response to my talking about constitutional rights such as the right to guns and free speech, please also remember that you’re not allowed to shoot anyone in a theater either. There’s no restriction to anyone yelling fire in a theater; however, if you do so, you’ll probably be arrested, indicted, and prosecuted. But, when it comes to the Constitution, Rights do not come with get out of jail free cards if you break the law, commit a crime, initiate a stampede, assault someone, shoot someone, or commit murder. So, apples and oranges. Just in case that’s your angle of attack. Most people will back down because it sounds logical, but it’s not. Try something else.

item.title: Chapter 253: Nowhere to run to, nowhere to hide
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator warns that all the public vitriol of 2016 to 2021 will be found and used against people, citing a judicial confirmation hearing.
item.content:encoded: All that public venom and vitriol that everyone spat gladly from 2016-2021 will most assuredly all bite us in our collective asses. Ask appeals court nominee Jennifer Sung about her confirmation hearing. All will always be revealed and used against you with extreme prejudice. It’s inevitable.

item.title: Chapter 252: When “Nazi!” is no longer a kill shot
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator notes that insults like Nazi or white supremacist no longer shame the right, and asks what comes next when insults become badges.
item.content:encoded: I don’t know if “Nazi,” “white supremacist,” or “literally Hitler” bothers or shames the right anymore. That’s why they’re actually calling themselves “pureblood” for having not received the coronavirus vaccine. What do you do when your insults become empowerments? What is the next step? The next move. When calling someone a Nazi only receives an eye roll? Yikes.

item.title: Chapter 251: Nobody cares about climate change nearly enough
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator doubts people will make wartime sacrifices for climate, giving up travel, meat and cars, especially when the rich ignore the rules.
item.content:encoded: I still don’t think anyone personally cares enough to actually do anything that would require extreme personal sacrifice, the kind the Brits and the Americans suffered during the world wars, domestically. Sacrificing products, services, cars, tires, nylon, meat, petrol/gas, etc, etc. To sacrifice travel, flying, tourism, vacations. An enforced global pandemic could barely shut down and quarantine people. Plus, rich people always cheat a lot on pleb rules, restrictions, and laws.

item.title: Chapter 250: Authoritarianism for public safety is still authoritarianism
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A thought experiment: safety is the perfect justification for authoritarian rule, since nobody wants to argue against protecting widows and orphans.
item.content:encoded: Thought experiment: authoritarianism for public safety is still authoritarianism, especially since “keeping you safe” is a most excellent way for authoritarians to enact authoritarianism. It’s a perfect system. Who doesn’t want to feel—and be—safer? Who doesn’t want to protect widows and orphans? Monsters! It’s genius! I mean, theoretically.

item.title: Chapter 249: Repent sinner
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: After hearing 9/11 compared to January 6th on NPR, the narrator predicts America will turn its war on terror inward against its own rural people.
item.content:encoded: Twelve times this morning, on only NPR, 9/11 was compared to and conflated with January 6th. I can predict where all of this is going. It’s going inwards. America will be the next Afghanistan, methinks. Repent sinner (and, by sinner, I mean, probably, Trumpers of any stripe). Rural and mountain people as the new Taliban, I’m afraid. It’s happening, people… Repent, repent!

item.title: Chapter 248: Dear illogical talking heads on the brink of two decades post-9/11
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that militants may be less likely to attack America once the occupation ends, since drone strikes and bombs feed terrorism.
item.content:encoded: Dear illogical talking heads on the brink of two decades post-9/11: don’t you think that radical Islamic militants might be less likely to commit terrorist acts on American soil now that we’re defeated and have left? When I’m occupied and being peppered with missiles and bombs by traumatic drones and aviation, I’m more likely to resort to asymmetric warfare that includes destination terrorism. Not the other way around. Actually attacking us on our soil would be unproductive. We’re vengeful.

item.title: Chapter 247: Too early to be grateful
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator reflects that gratitude is hard when everything built is taken away, whether by war, disaster or the loss of someone that you love.
item.content:encoded: I guess it’s too early to be grateful for those 20-years. I mean, most of the region never even had any of that. It’s hard to be grateful at all when everything you’ve built is stolen from you, though. That’s too true after floods, fires, hurricanes, tornadoes, and earthquakes, as well. Any devastation, really. Also, after a family member is taken from you. Any life-rocking loss, grief, trauma.

item.title: Chapter 246: Did America completely brain drain Afghanistan?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator asks whether evacuating pro democracy Afghans left the country without its educated reformers, leaving only fundamentalists behind.
item.content:encoded: Serious question: did America completely brain drain Afghanistan with our exfil of all the pro-democracy citizens who collaborated during the US occupation? So, will the result be a dearth of classically liberal democratic vision? Will the country now be bereft of their enlightenment egalitarians? Their social justice class? Are there only fundamentalist extremists left? What’s the story, morning glory? Shadow governing from self-imposed exile?

item.title: Chapter 245: Red, blue, black, brown, yellow, red, pink, rainbow
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A one sentence entry: if blue America knew how little red America thinks about race and identity, it would be amazed, insulted and appalled.
item.content:encoded: If blue only knew how little red ever thinks of black, brown, yellow, red, pink, or rainbow folks they would be amazed, insulted, and appalled.

item.title: Chapter 244: Donald Trump was the worst Adolf Hitler ever
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that despite comparisons to Hitler, Trump’s term brought no death camps or pogroms, only protest, and calls the comparison weak.
item.content:encoded:
Trump was the worst literally Adolf Hitler in history. I’m just a watcher. I know Trump said terrible things every day but it’s more about the doing than the fearing, fretting, or the existential threat.

No death camps, no pogroms, no journalists in reëducation camps, no killing fields, no yellow stars, no mobs disappearing people, no assassinations, no public beheading, no crucifixions, no public killings, no arms chopped off, no public burnings, and no more mass incarceration than normal, vanilla, everyday, America crimes against humanity.

Nothing except pride protests and defiant protests and not my president protests and pussy hat protests and rioters released and autonomy zones and favela encampments.

Trump sucked as the worst person in the world. He was all talk. I mean, Jan 6th was really disappointing for being literal Hitler! I mean, not even one single rifle, bomb, or even a fire or a Molotov cocktail.

item.title: Chapter 243: To Tell the Afghanistan Truth
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: Like the game show To Tell the Truth, the narrator asks which Afghanistan is real: tribes, city intellectuals, the government, or the Taliban.
item.content:encoded: There was/is a game show called To Tell the Truth. You have to choose which contestant is the actual person the moderator describes. I think of Afghanistan like this. Who is Afghanistan? The rural tribes? The city intellectuals? The American-supported Government? The Taliban? Everyone’s saying “it’s their Afghanistan” and “we’re Afghanistan” but I think they all are. How does that game work? Who wins? Who can win? How can it be win, win? Non-zero sum? It’s aiming to be a zero-sum game, methinks.

item.title: Chapter 242: Biden blames Trump for Not Getting Marines Killed?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator is confused by blaming Trump for a deal that he says protected servicemen, after thirteen died in the Kabul airport bombing in 2021.
item.content:encoded: So confounded. I don’t understand anything. I don’t know how saying Trump prevented the deaths of servicemen by making a deal with the Taliban is “blame” because it sounds like Trump protected the lives of servicemen rather than losing 12 in two suicide bombings. That’s a pretty heavy spin. “I blame Trump for not getting any Marines killed during his administration” sounds pretty weak. I don’t understand anything. So confused.

item.title: Chapter 241: America could win the Afghan war with crimes against humanity
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues America lost because winning would have required atrocities it had no will to commit, and because it never truly moved in.
item.content:encoded: We only “lost” because we didn’t have the nerve to win. “Winning” would require all the war crimes and crimes against humanity. We could have nuked, razed, decimated, and counter-terrorized our way into winning the war in Afghanistan. We could have pulled an Israel, a Russia. Those countries always punish terrorist acts against their people with punishing blows way out of proportion to the damage done. Shock and awe, every time. To the point of putting the fear of God even into fundamentalist Muslim jihadis. Even them. Plus, of course, no will, no buy-in, and no way to define success. What do you think? Plus, we invaded them. The only real way to win that type of war is to move in. Did we want to move in? It all came down to saving Muslim ladies and girls. No war has been won with that slogan. No, not even Nazi Germany. America didn’t fight the Western front to save those people in the camps and America didn’t fight the Eastern front to prevent Japan from their war crimes against the Chinese and Pacific Islanders. “There has never been a protracted war from which a country has benefited.”—Sun Tzu

item.title: Chapter 240: Still Saving Pagan Babies in 2021
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator compares the American occupation of Afghanistan to Spanish conquistadors, saving souls and civilizing natives by force of arms.
item.content:encoded: It’s pretty easy to reframe America’s uninvited invasion, occupation, and nation-building of Afghanistan. In order to prove just how imperial our having been in Afghanistan for the last 20-years, rebuilding the country in our own image, is, please do the following thought experiment. Please release your imagination and walk with me for a bit… Just replace George W Bush, Barack Obama, Donald Trump, and Joe Biden with Hernán Cortés, Francisco Pizarro, Christopher Columbus, and Pope Alexander VI; replace US Armed Forces with conquistadors; and replace Afghanis—women, girls, boys, elders—with Aztecs, Mayans, Amerindians, Mapuche people; then, replace soul-saving, civilizing, modernizing, and enculturating, with…. the same words. Does that make more sense as to why supporting the invasion and occupation of Afghanistan in order to save them from themselves is perfectly analogous to supporting the British colonization of the Americas in order to modernize and civilize the American Indians? A reminder, we were at war with Afghanistan during which at least 240,000 Afghans have died, many of them civilians—over the last 20-years; and, how many of those Afghans were women and girls?

item.title: Chapter 239: Look at how women in Afghanistan are treated! Outrageous!
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator shares the outrage over Afghan women’s treatment but argues drones and occupation could never change a fundamentalist culture there.
item.content:encoded: Yes, it’s outrageous. Appalling. I’m also outraged that we actually thought we could change their radical and radicalized fundamentalist culture with drones, bombs, troops, and occupation. Let’s invade and bomb Saudi now. I wonder how many of the 71k civilians who died during our war were girls and women? How did Afghanistan, Iran, Lebanon, etc, become women-friendly Westernized nations from the 1920s-1970s? And, how did they go from skirts and uncovered hair to fundamentalist Muslim countries? How do we get back there without the body count? Is our aggression against the Middle East exacerbating Islamic fundamentalism? Is Western imperialism a positive influence or is it perceived as the tip of the spear known as religious war, Christendom versus Islam?

item.title: Chapter 238: How will the Taliban fly the left behind Blackhawks?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator answers that Afghan pilots trained by the US military, hired contractors, or Pakistani allies could fly the aircraft left behind.
item.content:encoded: Just ask all the helio pilots we trained of those 300,000 US-military-trained soldiers who now fight for the Mujahedin. They know how to fly planes, too, and they know how to service them. Or, they can take the billions of dollars and hire Academi consultants and trainers. Or, maybe, just ask their Pakistani friends to be their pilots.

item.title: Chapter 237: Darkness Will Engulf the World!
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short entry suggesting that for ten years leaders have used natural threats to convince people they are to blame and only experts can save them.
item.content:encoded: If I didn’t know any better, I would say that the last ten years have been a game of ECLIPSE: find terrible, existentially threatening, naturally occurring phenomena and convince Stupid People that A) they are responsible for them and B) that the Smart People can save them.

item.title: Chapter 236: NPR Warhawks
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short entry in which the narrator is gobsmacked to hear NPR correspondents sound strongly in favor of staying at war in Afghanistan in 2021.
item.content:encoded: Gobsmacked as to how pro-Afghanistan war NPR News correspondents are this morning. The so-called liberal elite mainstream media is extremely pro-war today. It kind of breaks my brain. Warhawks for days!

item.title: Chapter 235: Train thy enemy
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator suggests the 300,000 Afghan soldiers America trained were mostly learning to fight the next superpower that invades their country.
item.content:encoded: Those 300,000 Afghani soldiers weren’t our allies, they were just learning how to be better soldiers against imperial invaders for the next time a superpower forgets history and decides to again attempt to tame the Graveyard of Empires™ (Last time, got training by both Spetsnaz and the Green Berets. This time, the Navy Seals!) That’ll show the next invading army!

item.title: Chapter 234: Graveyard of empires
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues America invaded Afghanistan for revenge after 9/11, and Afghans endure every invader by adapting and simply waiting them out.
item.content:encoded: America didn’t go to Afghanistan to help women and girls or to bolster some liberal democratic government. America invaded Afghanistan in knee-jerk response to 9/11 and to hunt down Osama bin Laden. An invaded Afghani people who have suffered invader after invader simply adapts, appeases, profits, trains, grins, bears it, and waits until coffers drain and public support wanes. Then, count the money, inventory assets and spoils, then revert until the next empire forgets historical precedent.

item.title: Chapter 233: Déjà Afghanistan
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short entry quoting Rudyard Kipling’s lines about a wounded soldier left on Afghanistan’s plains, offered as a comment on the American withdrawal.
item.content:encoded:
Déjà vu

“When you’re wounded and left on Afghanistan’s plains, and the women come out to cut up what remains, jest roll to your rifle and blow out your brains and go to your gawd like a soldier.”

—Rudyard Kipling

item.title: Chapter 232: Nazis and Wokies Sitting in a Tree K-I-S-S-I-N-G
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues the woke left and Nazis feed on each other, and that to him any tyrant of any race or ideology can rightly be called a Nazi.
item.content:encoded:
It’s not just the Nazis who love to wag their fingers at the woke left. The woke left loves all this finger waving at the Nazis.

The difference between you and me, probably, is that you have a coded right and wrong and I am stateless. To me, right and wrong are 100% POV, relative, and often related to power structures and grand agendas.

Any tyrant, to me, is a Nazi. Not just white guys.

To me, there can be African Nazis and there can be South Asian Nazis and Southeast Asian Nazis and there can be Pacific Islander Nazis and Mongolian Nazis and Middle Eastern Nazis (House of Saud), and Latin American Nazis. Also, Communist Nazis (Nationalsozialismus), etc.

Who gets to choose what is right and what is wrong? Who is right or wrong? Who the good Nazis are (are there good Nazis? The Nazis you know are better than the Nazis you don’t?)

The difference is that you believe that YOU get to choose. That you’re the beneficiary of the Book of Good and Bad. As I said, things that were forbidden only yesterday are beyond reproach today. Black Trans Women are Holy now (yes!) but for how long? Forever?

This strict concept of what’s absolutely good or bad can quickly be coöpted by the same people “you” ruled against the last time ’round. Right now, the terrorists are domestic white men; next time ’round it’s Mexicans, Muslims, Blacks, Jews, Gays.

It’s extremely easy for Very Powerful Tools and Very Powerful Weapons to be used against the Maker. The Patriot Act was a huge mistake. The Laws passed after 9/11 were inexcusable.

I guess I need to pop this in here as a de facto cliche trope:

“Those who would give up essential Liberty, to purchase a little temporary Safety, deserve neither Liberty nor Safety.”

If you carry a gun for your own safety beware of knowing how to protect yourself from having it taken away from you and used against you.

I am a gun owner and it’s never easy to prevent an attacker from disarming you and shooting your own face off.

It takes a lot of training and an insane amount of understanding as to the gravity of engaging in deadly force.

item.title: Chapter 231: Germany is always either extremely Fascist or Antifaschistische
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: Drawing on his years in Berlin, the narrator argues that the same German trust in rules that enabled fascism now drives its fierce antifascism.
item.content:encoded:
I lived in Berlin from 2008-2011 and the exact thing that made them extremely vulnerable to Fascism is the same quality that makes them hard-core Antifaschistische as well. Knowing what’s “right” and “wrong” and their painfully innocent trust of their government and brands they’re still extreme nationalists but realize they can only fetishize their cities, not their country, so they do that.

They fetishize their Siemens and their Bayers, they exhibit their superiority through moral virtue instead of their occult metaphysical obsession with Nature so, like any other way too homogenous culture, or addict, they just glom on to another addiction.

The Berlin I lived in was so actively contrite over Nazism that there were anti-Nazi docs on TV every day and restrictions of depictions everywhere.

The problem is that once Germany feels like it earned its way out of die Hundehütte, it’ll have no more fucks to give. It was happening when I was there back in 2008-2011 in the South. Rebuilding cities to pre-war, spec, erasing WW2, returning to the 15th-19th century if you’ll remember your history, it wasn’t only Jews but also anyone who was inconsistent with the German concept of itself, which is really inspired by a German Romantic and Naturphilosophie movement conceit of self which is really amusing.

This next time, maybe not about European Jews but surely about Muslims and immigrants and North Africans and Syrians and even, possibly Romanians and Eastern Europeans and Slavs and Africans. Who knows. Nazis who become anti-Nazis with such vigor are always to not be trusted.

item.title: Chapter 230: Are you actually pro free speech and pro democracy?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that supporting free speech means defending speech you hate, and that putting justice above free speech should be admitted openly.
item.content:encoded:
If you’re pro free speech but want to punch Nazis marching through your Main Street then maybe you’re a hypocrite.

Who decides what’s poison? Who decides?

Fighting book banning cannot only work if you get to fight the banning of just your books. Using the excuse of needing to dismantle the patriarchy isn’t a good enough reason if you’re pro free speech.

You don’t have to be pro free speech or liberty, you can say that civil rights and social justice trumps freedom, liberty, and freedom of speech, but be honest about it.

There are surely extremists the world over, including Christians, who put their Bible ahead of freedom, liberty, egalitarianism, or free speech, so you don’t have to pretend that you’re pro free speech.

You don’t even have to say that you’re actually pro-democracy. Why? Because democracy is a neutral medium. What the most people vote for goes. That doesn’t remotely guarantee enlightenment, humanist, liberal, socially just, values.

So many despotisms who have been liberated of their despot (through American interventionism) have used their democracy to vote in an extremist Mullah. True story. Has happened a bunch.

So, if you want to leverage some good old fashioned Cultural Revolutionary tough love until we reach some sort of progressive utopia, just be a lot more open, honest, transparent, and truthful as to your wants and needs. Be honest, freedom of speech and democracy never turns out right because of the entire popularity thing.

Right?

Life is exactly like high school and nothing’s ever changed. Same world. You’ll really just need to make us with extreme prejudice, by any means necessary.

item.title: Chapter 229: Stop using girls and women as political props
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator notes that the welfare of Afghan women became a talking point only at withdrawal, and suspects it is being used as a political gambit.
item.content:encoded: You know who you’ve never heard a peep about in the last 20 years? How well the women and girls were doing. Now, it’s a ubiquitous talking point. If I were a cynical man, I’d think this was a political strategy. Do it for the women, do it for the girls. Afghanistan never became 60s Tehran in the last 20 years. This feels like a gambit. Color me suspicious.

item.title: Chapter 228: It’s a terrible time to be a climate activist
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that the threat of dying from COVID now makes dying from climate change later a hard sell, in a country that fails marshmallow tests.
item.content:encoded: It’s a terrible time to be a climate activist because the threat of dying today from COVID-19 takes the wind out of the sails of dying tomorrow. People might even live harder, faster, dirtier, smoggier, make more babies, do more travel, buy faster cars just to celebrate being alive. Alan Furst said “live today, for tomorrow we die” and not “conserve today, for we might die in thirty years.” It’s a really hard sell to a country that fails every marshmallow test ever invented.

item.title: Chapter 227: Aegrescit medendo
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: An Army officer friend says Vietnam and Afghanistan were winnable only through atrocities, and the narrator applies Virgil’s line to street crime.
item.content:encoded: My Army LTC friend told me that Vietnam and Afghanistan were totally winnable but the cost to both the soldiers, the enemy, and civilians was too dear for public and world opinion to stomach. To win would require the sort of razing that crimes against humanity are made of. Same thing with America’s out-of-control street crime and gang violence. Even saying “gang violence” rings of racism. Any solution is untenable. To be that guy who quotes Virgil, “The remedy is worse than the disease.”

item.title: Chapter 226: Loutish German soccer hooligans singing soccer shanties.
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: After a year in Berlin, the narrator meets loutish suburban German soccer fans singing shanties on the trains, far from the cultured Germans he imagined.
item.content:encoded: I lived in Berlin for a year before I was at Hauptbahnhof right at the perfect time to realize that not all Germans were urbane, sophisticated, extremely cultured, and even painfully lovely. There were suburban German hooligans everywhere with their milk crates filled with pilsner on the S and U being all loutish and singing soccer shanties.

item.title: Chapter 225: Folks know that guns are for killing humans
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator asks what gun death statistics include and argues gun owners know guns are for defense, so talk of defunding police sells more guns.
item.content:encoded: Do homicides include suicides? Do they include legal defensive shootings? Or do they only include intentional gun killings? I think most gun owners know what their guns are intentionally made to do and have come to understand when and why they would use them. I wonder if any of this would dissuade people who never thought guns were for hunting or shooting sports in the first place. That’s why solid studies like this don’t catch: “of course guns are for defending oneself using lethal force, duh.” So, people who are in that space only see more gun crime obviously requiring more guns with which to defend themselves. Any mention of defunding police sells more guns. I’ve been following this since Gabby Giffords was shot. Her shooting sold every single Glock 19 in America. It’s a crazy paradox. It’s a fighting fire with fire mentality.

item.title: Chapter 224: History is always subjective
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that all history is edited and written with a goal, to unite or divide a people, like the Council of Nicaea shaping a record.
item.content:encoded: Every single bit of history is subjective, edited, intentional, and has a purpose transcending simple knowledge-sharing. Written by people and stitched together by a history of record council of Nicaea, if you will. With a goal. An endgame. Bring a people together, tear them apart; unite them, sow strife; realign culture, integrate cultures, or dissolve one. Don’t play coy.

item.title: Chapter 223: January 6th was the worst American Reichstag Fire ever
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that January 6th was a weak Reichstag fire, with selfies instead of guns, and questions claims about how many people died.
item.content:encoded:
January 6th is the worst Reichstag Fire event anyone could have concocted. “Wanted to hang the Vice President,” “tried to kill Nancy Pelosi?” Really? Super-lame. Not even a little Capitol fire. Just insurrectionists doing selfies and making Facebook Lives, Instagrams, and TikToks.

In a country rife with black battle rifles, “there were guns back in the hotel room,” doesn’t really cut it. Nowadays, people actually believe that it was a truly armed insurrection and that 5 cops were killed in cold blood. The only person killed in cold blood was an “insurrectionist” herself. Social engineering FTW!

item.title: Chapter 222: The only reason to go offworld is for remittance money
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator predicts space work will be like oil rigs or submarines, done for money or science, not out of any dream of colonizing the stars.
item.content:encoded:
Getting a job offworld will be analogous to getting a job on an oil drilling platform. You only ever do anything like that for either the money, for remittance for your family, or for science.

Colonize other worlds? Spread humanity into the stars? Living anywhere else besides another earth will suck as much as living in a submarine.

Ever meet a submariner? They’re a different species. At best, like living in an Antarctic research center.

Ever seen their stir-crazy? How badly they want to return stateside? Or to Argentina or Australia? Or, ever meet a Seaman or Sailor stuck on a warship for months and months.

That’s what offworlding will be like. Only deplorables will be sent to space. It’ll be like when your parents tell you your old dog lives upstate on a nice farm. “We sent them to a better place with such better opportunities,” will be code for either depopulation or deportation.

item.title: Chapter 221: Useful idiots
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A useful idiot is someone who promotes a cause without grasping its goals; the narrator traces the Cold War term and the false Lenin attribution.
item.content:encoded:
In political jargon, a useful idiot is a derogatory term for a person perceived as propagandizing for a cause without fully comprehending the cause’s goals, and who is cynically used by the cause’s leaders. The term was originally used during the Cold War to describe non-communists regarded as susceptible to communist propaganda and manipulation. The term has often been attributed to Vladimir Lenin, but this attribution is unsubstantiated.

The phrase useful idiot has often been attributed to Vladimir Lenin, but he is not documented as ever having used the phrase. In a 1987 article for The New York Times, American journalist William Safire investigated the origin of the term, noting that a senior reference librarian at the Library of Congress had been unable to find the phrase in Lenin’s works and concluding that in the absence of new evidence, the term could not be attributed to Lenin.[3][4] Similarly, the Oxford English Dictionary in defining useful idiot says: “The phrase does not seem to reflect any expression used within the Soviet Union”.

The term appeared in a June 1948 New York Times article on contemporary Italian politics (“Communist shift is seen in Europe”), citing the centrist social democratic Italian paper L’Umanità. L’Umanità wrote that left-wing social democrats, who had entered into a popular front with the Italian Communist Party during the 1948 elections, would be given the option to either merge with the Communists or leave the alliance. The term was later used in a 1955 article in the American Federation of Labor News-Reporter to refer to Italians who supported Communist causes. Time first used the phrase in January 1958, writing that some Italian Christian Democrats considered social activist Danilo Dolci a “useful idiot” for Communist causes. It has since recurred in that periodical’s articles.

A similar term, useful innocents, appears in a 1946 Reader’s Digest article titled “Yugoslavia’s Tragic Lesson to the World”, written by Bogdan Raditsa. Raditsa had served the Yugoslav government-in-exile during World War II, supported Josip Broz Tito’s partisans (though not a Communist himself) and briefly served in Tito’s new Yugoslav government before leaving for New York. “In the Serbo-Croat language”, says Raditsa, “the communists have a phrase for true democrats who consent to collaborate with them for [the sake of] ‘democracy’. It is Korisne Budale, or Useful Innocents.” In his 1947 book, Planned Chaos, Austrian-American economist Ludwig von Mises writes that the term useful innocents was used by Communists for liberals, whom von Mises describes as “confused and misguided sympathizers”.

In 1959, Congressman Ed Derwinski of Illinois entered an editorial by the Chicago Daily Calumet into the Congressional record, referring to Americans who traveled to the Soviet Union to promote peace as “what Lenin calls useful idiots in the Communist game”. In 1961, American journalist Frank Gibney wrote that Lenin had coined the phrase useful idiot. Gibney wrote that the phrase was a good description of “Communist follower[s]” from Jean-Paul Sartre to left-wing socialists in Japan to members of the Chilean Popular Front. In a speech in 1965, Spruille Braden, an American diplomat who was stationed in a number of Latin American countries during the 1930s and 1940s and was later a lobbyist for the United Fruit Company, said the term was used by Joseph Stalin to refer to what Braden called “countless innocent although well-intentioned sentimentalists or idealists” who aided the Soviet agenda.

Writing in The New York Times in 1987, William Safire discussed the increasing use of the term useful idiot against “anybody insufficiently anti-Communist in the view of the phrase’s user”, including Congressmen who supported the anti-Contras Sandinistas in Nicaragua and the Dutch socialists. After President Ronald Reagan concluded negotiations with Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev over the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, conservative political leader Howard Phillips declared Reagan a “useful idiot for Soviet propaganda.”

item.title: Chapter 220: Trump is just the pupu platter
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator predicts deeper conflict whether or not Trump stays, calling him a warning of what is still coming rather than the doom itself.
item.content:encoded: Trump is just the pupu platter for what’s to come, whether or not Trump falls dead tomorrow. I’m pretty sure some sort of civil war or white cultural bloodbath will happen either way. Trump is just a best case scenario warning for things to come. He’s a harbinger; he’s not the doom itself.

item.title: Chapter 219: Raising a Trump flag or poster isn’t about Donald Trump anymore
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that Trump flags are now chosen to provoke, a signifier like other defiant flags, more than a statement about Trump himself.
item.content:encoded: Raising a Trump flag is intentionally chosen because it triggers people, it’s defiant, it is bombastic, and it’s basically as audacious as the swastika or the battle flag of the confederacy or even the American flag to some people or the don’t tread on me snake. Signifiers.

item.title: Chapter 218: Whatever happened to code-switching?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator recalls when code switching, speaking the dominant culture while keeping your own, was encouraged, and asks where that idea went.
item.content:encoded:
I remember when code switching was a thing.

When one was encouraged to both speak the culture of the lingua franca as well as maintaining and growing and building one’s own culture.

I guess there needs to be an entire FUBU subculture built and maintained, separate but equal. I guess there already is, right?

item.title: Chapter 217: If anti-racism rejects default culture what’s embraced instead?
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: A short follow-up asking what is embraced instead if antiracism rejects the dominant culture, since that culture still governs school and work.
item.content:encoded: But it also means you won’t fit into school or the meritocracy or university or into business or into genteel society or polite society or even out of jail.

item.title: Chapter 216: Is anti-racism anti-assimilation
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator calls antiracism a necessary step for America, then asks whether it also rejects assimilation into a single shared American culture.
item.content:encoded: I do see anti-racism as a mandatory step in the American experiment. Question, though: is antiracism also anti-assimilation? I perceive the movement as a deconstruction—a rejection—of the American dream cultural consensus reality. As, by definition, racist, white supremacist, and anti-Black. Am I on the right path?

item.title: Chapter 215: Germans made Hitler; Americans make Trump
item.dc:creator: Chris Abraham
item.description: The narrator argues that strongmen like Hitler or Trump are symptoms of mass feeling, filling a gap that a public creates, not the cause of it.
item.content:encoded:
They’re symptoms not causes. It’s not just to not blame the Germans and the Americans. Don’t let them off the hook. Hitler might have been a true believer but Trump’s probably not.
